items.title: EASA Scientific Committee publishes its Annual Report
items.summary: The EASA Scientific Committee (SciCom) Annual Report 2025 is now available. This report covers the Committee’s fourth year of operation, and presents the activities undertaken, key achievements, and recommendations for future work.

items.title: EASA modernises flight simulation training devices’ rules to support innovation and future pilot training
items.summary: COLOGNE, July 15 2026 - The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has introduced a new regulatory framework for Flight Simulation Training Devices (FSTDs), marking the most significant evolution of flight simulation qualification in Europe in decades.

items.title: EASA updates Easy Access Rules for Third Country Operators
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has published Revision from July 2026 of the Easy Access Rules for Third Country Operators (EAR for TCO).

items.title: EASA releases tool to assess the noise levels of light propeller-driven aeroplanes
items.summary: ENCODE, “EASA's Noise Compliance Demonstration Evaluator”, is an MS Excel tool that can be used to calculate the noise level and confidence interval from data measured during a noise test performed in accordance with Chapter 10 of ICAO Annex 16, Volume I. The tool validates each individual test run against the limitations for environmental conditions and performance.

items.title: Protecting the backbone of aviation: EASA and EUROCONTROL host workshop on Europe’s GNSS interference Action Plan
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency and EUROCONTROL joined forces this week, hosting a workshop with more than 100 experts from across the aviation sector to discuss the response to the growing operational impact of Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) across European and neighbouring airspace.

items.title: EASA issues AD 2026-0134 superseding Emergency Airworthiness Directive 2025-0268-E for Airbus 320 family
items.summary: EASA has issued AD 2026-0134 for certain A320 family aeroplanes, which was previously published for public consultation as PAD 26-050, and which supersedes Emergency Airworthiness Directive (EAD) 2025-0268-E. The EAD was issued on November 28, 2025 to address a susceptibility introduced by a software update in one of its onboard computers. It addressed an issue which manifested itself in an event on JetBlue flight 1230 on October 30, 2025.

items.title: Revised conflict zone advisories for Middle East
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA), working with the European Commission and the Member States, has adapted the EU conflict zones advisory for air operators on the Middle East in response to the latest developments in the region.

items.title: EASA Olympics for aviation AI-based systems — Now closed for entries
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has launched the AI Olympics — an initiative that goes hand in hand with the EASA AI Days conference taking place in Cologne on September 9 — 10, 2026. If you have a great aviation AI-based system, we are offering you the chance to show the industry what you are developing and to present it at the event.

items.title: EASA updates Safety Information Bulletin on GNSS interference
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has updated its Safety Information Bulletin (SIB) on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) Outage and Alterations Leading to Navigation / Surveillance Degradation. SIB 2022-02 was first published on March 17, 2022 and the last update was Revision 3 on July 5, 2024. Revision 4 was published July 3, 2026.

items.title: Aviation Non-CO₂ Expert Network furthers discussions on climate impacts from non-CO₂ emissions
items.summary: The 7th Plenary Meeting of the Aviation Non-CO₂ Expert Network (ANCEN) brought together sixty leading experts representing the scientific community, academia, aircraft manufacturers and operators, fuel producers, research organisations, air navigation service providers, non-governmental organisations, regulators and policymaking actors to advance the understanding of aviation’s climate impacts from non-CO₂ emissions and support evidence-based discussions and decision-making.

items.title: EASA publishes new Easy Access Rules for European Technical Standard Orders
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has published Amendment 16 and Amendment 15 of the Easy Access Rules (EAR) for European Technical Standard Orders (CS-ETSO) in pdf format. Today's publication also includes corrected versions of the published Amendments 11-14 of the EAR for ETSO, also in pdf.

items.title: EASA Certification Platform goes live
items.summary: The new EASA Certification Platform goes live! EASA has worked hard on the digitalisation of certification projects, and during the last 10 months has developed and tested a new platform designed to improve efficiency, transparency, and predictability in the way we work with external stakeholders in different Certification areas.

items.title: FAA and EASA pledge cooperation for the new era of aviation
A Simpler Digital Experience for MOA and MTOA Organisations
items.summary: Maintenance Organisation Approval (MOA) and Maintenance Training Organisation Approval (MTOA) holders can now benefit from a more streamlined and digital way of interacting with EASA through the Organisation Approvals Tool (OA Tool) and the EASA Service Portal.

items.title: New career opportunity: EASA Study Placement Scheme open for applications
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) has opened the Study Placement Scheme (SPS) for applications on the EASA Careers Portal. If you need to complete a compulsory placement or write your final thesis as part of your university studies or professional qualification, do not miss out on this opportunity! The call for this year is open until 31 December 2026.

items.title: EASA publishes Article 89 report on aviation safety and socio-economic factors
items.summary: COLOGNE, June 8, 2026 — The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) published an assessment of the interdependencies between aviation safety and socio-economic factors affecting safety-critical personnel in Europe, to ensure that socio-economic dimensions have been adequately integrated into aviation safety analysis.

items.title: EASA releases latest issue of its Concept Paper on Artificial Intelligence for comment
items.summary: The European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) released Proposed Issue 03 of its Concept Paper on Artificial Intelligence (AI), now open for a consultation period of 10 weeks. This is the final Concept Paper deliverable foreseen under the EASA Artificial Intelligence Roadmap 2.0.

items.title: Extended Deadline for CEI 2026.03 — Direct Accreditation of Qualified Entities: Air Traffic Management/Air Navigation Services Systems and Constituents domain experts
items.summary: EASA has extended the deadline for applications to the call for expression of interest (CEI): CEI Number: 2026.03Categories of Tasks: Air Traffic Management/Air Navigation Services Systems and ConstituentsExtended Closing Date: 14 June 2026 (23:59 CET) EASA seeks to accredit up to eight Qualified Entities.

items.title: Europe for Aviation strives for more modern and efficient ATM in Europe
items.summary: LISBON, May 29, 2026 — Nine European institutions showcased their joint vision and progress toward a more modern and effective air traffic management system in Europe at Airspace World, the annual three-day ATM trade fair that took place in Lisbon this week. items.title: EASA and EUROCONTROL release Electronic Conspicuity Use Cases for safer shared airspace
items.summary: EUROCONTROL and EASA, together with aviation stakeholders, have jointly developed two use case descriptions for the use of Electronic Conspicuity (EC) to enhance traffic awareness for pilots and facilitate integration of drones in shared airspace. The use cases will serve as input to the joint Electronic Conspicuity assessment and validation work performed in Europe and aim to support the safety of manned and unmanned aviation through affordable, interoperable and harmonised solutions.
